IN.tax_note: Approximate Indian new-regime burden at senior professional income levels.
IN.visa_note: No work visa required for an Indian citizen.

US.tax_note: Federal, payroll and typical state taxes vary widely.
US.visa_note: H-1B is capped and lottery-based unless the employer is cap-exempt; a better salary is not automatically obtainable.

GB.tax_note: Income tax plus national insurance at experienced tech salary levels.
GB.visa_note: Skilled Worker needs sponsorship; Global Talent can work but requires endorsement or prize evidence.

DE.tax_note: Income tax and social contributions for a single worker are high but include public benefits.
DE.visa_note: EU Blue Card is realistic for qualifying salary and degree-equivalent roles, but employer and documentation still matter.

SG.tax_note: Singapore income tax is comparatively low; CPF does not usually apply to foreign employees.
SG.visa_note: Employment Pass approval uses COMPASS and employer sponsorship; strong pay helps but does not guarantee approval.

CA.visa_note: Employer work permits and Express Entry are possible but slower than accepting an India/remote role.

AU.tax_note: Income tax plus Medicare levy estimate.
AU.visa_note: Skilled and employer-sponsored visas exist, but occupation lists, points and sponsorship decide feasibility.

AE.tax_note: No federal personal income tax; estimate leaves room for fees and mandatory costs.
AE.visa_note: Work residency is employer-sponsored; easier than lottery systems but tied to the job.
